graph_cut_binary — SEGMENTATION graph op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.graph_cut_binary(image, *, lam: 'float' = 1.0, mu_bg: 'Optional[float]' = None, mu_fg: 'Optional[float]' = None, contrast_sigma: 'Optional[float]' = None, seeds=None, connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import seggraph; seggraph.graph_cut_binary(image, *, lam: 'float' = 1.0, mu_bg: 'Optional[float]' = None, mu_fg: 'Optional[float]' = None, contrast_sigma: 'Optional[float]' = None, seeds=None, connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("graph_cut_binary"))

Usage

Binary graph cut (Boykov–Jolly 2001): minimises E = Σ_p D_p(x_p) + λ Σ w_pq [x_p ≠ x_q] exactly by max-flow / min-cut (graph_cut_binary).

The data terms are D_p(0) = (I_p − μ_bg)², D_p(1) = (I_p − μ_fg)² (if μ is omitted, it is the mean of two groups of isodata). The weight of the side is w_pq = exp(−(I_p − I_q)²/(2σ²)) / dist(p, q)(contrast_sigma = σ, omitting 1/dist = Potts). seeds is labels2d 1 = background species, 2 = object species. The constraint weight is 1 + max_p Σ_q λ w_pq + max_p |D_p(0)-D_p(1)| And it also exceeds the data term difference of free pixels (not counted as energy).

Returns: mask(object = True), energy = data + smooth, cut_value / flow_value(value converted to real number = integer value / scale + constant), cut_value_int / flow_value_int (maximum flow = minimum cut gate), quantization_bound (quantization of real numbers by integerization) Upper bound on the difference from the minimum, 0 for integer input).
